name: thin-job
about: An opening with one fact and no description: few honest angles exist.

area.label: Fixture Yard, IL
area.reason: Fixture: drivers within a day's drive of the yard.

history.text: Boostpoint 2026 benchmark, CDL drivers on Meta: an ad costing more than $42.00 per lead after 5 leads, or $85.00 spent with no lead, is where pausing is suggested.

output.audience: Drivers who already hold a CDL and are driving now or looking for a seat. They want to see what the job pays per week before they bother to call. A plainly stated pay amount per week is what would make them stop on this ad.

angles.idea: Lead with the pay per week, stated plainly, over a truck moving down the road.
angles.proof: The opening states its pay as an amount per week.
angles.why: The pay per week is the only term the job states, so it leads. This carrier has no ad history; nothing has been measured, format included, so judge it against the benchmark cost per lead.

angles.idea: Lead with what knowing the pay per week means for planning at home, with the amount close behind.
angles.proof: The job states pay as an amount per week, so a driver can see it before applying.
angles.why: The job states no schedule, so this angle rests on the pay per week alone and must promise nothing beyond it. Nothing has been measured for this carrier, format included.

angles.idea: Lead with a parked truck waiting for a CDL driver, then state the pay per week; make no claim about the truck itself.
angles.proof: The opening is for a CDL driver and it states its pay as an amount per week.
angles.why: The job gives no equipment facts, so the truck is the picture and the open CDL seat is the message. Nothing has been measured for this carrier, format included.
